name: NSA Special Source Operations

summary.text: Special Source Operations is the NSA division that, according to the June 2013 Washington Post and Guardian reporting on documents leaked by Edward Snowden, runs the PRISM programme of collection from U.S. internet companies under Section 702 of FISA. Press descriptions of the leaked slides say 'Special Source Operations' refers to the agency's alliances with trusted U.S. companies, and that a slide titled 'Dates When PRISM Collection Began For Each Provider' lists Microsoft first, with a start date of September 11, 2007. Microsoft has said it provides customer data only in response to legally binding orders.

facts.claim: Press accounts of the leaked NSA slides describe 'Special Source Operations' as the term for the agency's alliances with trusted U.S. companies.
facts.quote: the term refers to alliances with trusted U.S. companies

facts.claim: A leaked slide titled 'Dates When PRISM Collection Began For Each Provider' lists Microsoft first, with a collection start date of September 11, 2007, followed in later years by Yahoo, Google, Facebook, Paltalk, Skype, AOL and Apple.
facts.quote: lists Microsoft first, with a collection start date of Sept. 11, 2007

facts.claim: Microsoft responded to the PRISM reports by saying it provides customer data only when it receives a legally binding order or subpoena and that it did not take part in any broader voluntary national security programme.
facts.quote: Microsoft said it provides customer data only when it receives a legally binding order or subpoena and that it did not take part in any broader voluntary national security program.

facts.claim: At a March 2014 Privacy and Civil Liberties Oversight Board hearing, NSA General Counsel Rajesh De said service providers know of and receive legal compulsion for the NSA's collection of communications data under Section 702, including collection in transit.
facts.quote: service providers also know and receive legal compulsions surrounding NSA's harvesting of communications data directly in transit under Section 702

connections.claim: Leaked NSA slides list Microsoft as the first PRISM provider, with collection beginning September 11, 2007; Microsoft says it complies only with legally binding orders.

openQuestions: The site's statement that Microsoft was the first company listed as a PRISM provider in September 2007 is supported by press descriptions of the leaked slide. The slides themselves (Washington Post, June 2013) and the PCLOB's July 2014 Section 702 report were not reachable and should be added as primary sources.
The site also lists 'PRISM program office' as a separate entity; the sources treat PRISM as a programme run within Special Source Operations rather than as a distinct office.
